shared_elements: upright freestanding stone monolith with rounded/domed top
low-relief carving on a flattened frontal face
justification: Both are tall, rounded-topped stone slabs bearing shallow relief on a single frontal face, and both include concentric circular discs and curling scroll-like elements, which gives them a broadly similar silhouette and material presence. The decisive difference is organisation and scale of carving: A is a tightly ruled grid of small, densely detailed rectangular blocks covering a framed panel, whereas B is a single sparse, large-scale figural/anthropomorphic composition with a carved face and body markings on an unframed boulder.
